newsitem.title: USA: Echlin sees Q3, full-year earnings down.
newsitem.headline: Echlin sees Q3, full-year earnings down.

text.p: Echlin Inc on Thursday projected grim financial results for the 1997 third quarter, saying it expects to see a 20 to 25 percent decline in earnings per share.

The forecast referred to last year's $0.70 per share third quarter figure. For the full fiscal year ending August 31, earnings will likely be 10 to 15 percent lower than 1996's $2.30 per share, excluding any one-time gains or charges, the company said in a statement.
Echlin president Larry McCurdy attributed most of the shortfall to continued soft demand in many markets.
Areas of particular softness are the North American aftermarket for engine system products, and the European original equipment market for heavy-duty brake parts, the company said.
In addition, the company said it was evaluating the consolidation of manufacturing plants and warehouses, and the possible sale of under-performing businesses.
The company predicted a fourth quarter charge for the restructuring of more than $100 million after tax.
Echlin makes and distributes motor brake, engine and steering system parts.
